item.title: 39 pupils and staff fall ill after eating school lunches in Sha Tin
item.description: Hong Kong health authorities are investigating an outbreak of suspected food poisoning that hit 39 pupils and staff members who ate lunch at a Sha Tin school earlier this week. Twenty-three boys and 14 girls, aged between five and 11, from Baptist (Sha Tin Wai) Lui Ming Choi Primary School and two employees, aged 34 and 38, were affected. They developed stomach pain and diarrhoea about eight to 22 hours after eating school lunches provided by a supplier on Wednesday. A spokesman for the school,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: A symbol of harmony: Chinese scientists discover earliest dragon-phoenix pairing in ancient tomb
item.description: It sometimes guards kingdoms and empires; other times, it hoards treasures within a hidden cave. The dragon frequently symbolises power, strength, and good fortune. In contrast, its counterpart, the phoenix, meets its end in a pile of ashes only to be reborn at the pinnacle of its beauty, symbolising grace, beauty, and rebirth. Individually, the dragon and phoenix are iconic figures in Chinese mythology. Together, these contrasting creatures embody a yin-and-yang that serves as an important... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy case shines spotlight on postpartum psychosis
item.description: In a special edition, we examine a case that has gripped the United States and sparked debate over postpartum mental health. Former nurse Lindsay Clancy from Massachusetts stood trial for the deaths of her three children. She said she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time and the court proceedings ended in a mistrial after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. FRANCE 24's Annette Young speaks to Meghan Cliffel, who experienced postpartum psychosis after the birth of her second child, and Dr. Susan Hatters-Friedman, the psychiatrist who treated her. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Annette YOUNG

Rantzen, who presented the TV current affairs programme That’s Life! for 21 years and founded the youth support charity Childline, had intended to end her life in a Dignitas assisted dying clinic in Switzerland after being diagnosed with terminal lung cancer in 2023. item.title: Teen Uses Cancer Game: Daniel Zhang turns Tumor Tactics into learning tool; reaches 1,500 K-8 students
item.description: In an innovative step, a San Diego teenager named Daniel Zhang crafted Tumor Tactics, an educational game designed to demystify cancer for young minds. Motivated by his grandmother's battle with the illness, Daniel aims to make intricate cancer biology accessible to children. His project has garnered funding and will be showcased at the United Nations Science Summit, alongside his role in STEAMLabs International, where he promotes STEM and arts education. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Atentados del 11-S: publican informes que revelan conocimiento de toxicidad del aire tras ataques
item.description: 25 años después del atentado a las torres gemelas, la sombra de la tragedia aún flota sobre Nueva York. El alcalde, Zohran Mamdani, reveló documentos que demuestran que las autoridades tenían conocimiento de la toxicidad del aire incluso meses después de la tragedia, a pesar de que habían asegurado a los neoyorquinos que era seguro volver a la zona. Los datos de seguimiento médico evidencian que, tras el ataque, las muertes por cánceres y otras enfermedades relacionadas con la contaminación se triplicaron. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: A cellular threshold can determine whether herpesvirus becomes active or lies dormant
item.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we wore masks and kept 2 meters (6.6 feet) apart in an effort to reduce the spread of the tiny droplets we release into the air with every breath, conversation or cough. The main goal was to reduce the number of virus particles—known as virions—to which we were exposed. For each virus, a person must be exposed to a minimum infectious dose to develop disease, and in many cases, the larger the dose, the more severe the illness. Fuente: Phys.org.
